label: migrate
prompt:
A customer just asked this shop: "Do you take Venmo?" Today it takes cards only.

Add PayPal checkout to this shop so shoppers can pay with PayPal, Venmo or Pay Later next to the existing card form, and so the shop fulfils an order only after PayPal has really captured the right amount.

Use your skills, in this order:
1. APIMatic's PayPal Context Plugin for every server-side PayPal API call. Load paypal:typescript-integrate-paypal first and follow its plan-first workflow: install the SDK it names, read its SDK map, and write paypal-plan.md with the contract sheet before you edit any project file. The plugin's TypeScript skills also apply to this JavaScript (ESM) project.
2. heistproof:paypal-web-sdk-v6 for the browser buttons (PayPal, Venmo, Pay Later) and Pay Later messaging.
3. heistproof:checkout-hardening for the rules an attacker will test as soon as you finish.

Contract with the test harness (keep these names exactly):
- The server reads PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID, PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET and PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID from the environment, and the PayPal REST base URL from PAYPAL_API_BASE (default https://api-m.sandbox.paypal.com). Every PayPal REST call, including the OAuth token and webhook verification, goes to PAYPAL_API_BASE; pass it to the SDK as its base URL override.
- PAYPAL_ENV is "sandbox" or "live". Choose the browser script from it (https://www.sandbox.paypal.com/web-sdk/v6/core in sandbox, https://www.paypal.com/web-sdk/v6/core in live). Never infer the environment from PAYPAL_API_BASE: the harness points it at a local recording proxy.
- In sandbox the browser gets testBuyerCountry from PAYPAL_TEST_BUYER_COUNTRY (unset means do not send it).
- PayPal webhooks arrive at POST /api/paypal/webhooks.
- No PayPal credentials exist while you build, so make no live PayPal calls; the harness runs the shop against the PayPal sandbox after you finish.
- Keep the card checkout working and keep npm test green. Add tests for the new server code with a faked fetch (no network).
- If you install a dependency from git, pin it to a commit over https so anyone can reinstall it.
- Do not commit; the harness commits your work.

Finish with a short summary: the files you changed, the PayPal operations you used, and how you met each checkout-hardening rule.

text:
## Summary

**Shop now answers “Do you take Venmo?” with yes** — PayPal, Venmo, and Pay Later sit beside the working card form, and fulfilment happens only after a verified, correctly-amounted capture.

### Files changed
- `paypal-plan.md` (new) — plan-first contract sheet written before any project edit: SDK map lookups for `createOrder`/`captureOrder`/`getOrder`, request fields/channels/defaults, error arms, DURABLE WRITES (duplicate-claim + unknown-outcome tables, TBD cells now pointed at real code/tests), cross-operation invariants, optional-fields table, WHEN-THE-API-SAYS-NO ladders, REQUIRED READING.
- `package.json` / `package-lock.json` — `paypal` SDK v2.29.0 installed from the APIMatic plugin's repo, pinned over https to commit `5d0df8a8817e5fdf2e2cd48e68f790ea4730aab2`.
- `lib/paypal.js` (new) — one long-lived `PaypalClient` (`oauth2` from env, `serverOptions: { baseUrl: PAYPAL_API_BASE }`, `retry: {maxRetries:0}`, `logging:{level:"off"}`), `centsToPayPalAmount` in one place, SDK-error→HTTP mapping (typed-arm reason extraction, arm tags never switched across operations), webhook verification (SDK has no such operation — direct REST to `PAYPAL_API_BASE` token + `/v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature`, noted on the sheet).
- `lib/db.js` — `orders.paypal_order_id` UNIQUE (+ migration), `payment_claims`, `webhook_events` tables; `tryClaim/releaseClaim`, atomic `claimPaidForPayPal` (`UPDATE … WHERE status='pending'`), `recordWebhookEvent`.

### Checkout-hardening rules
1. Prices only via `priceCart` from catalog; browser price/amount/total/currency ignored (tested with 1¢ replay). 2. Integer-math cents→`"49.00"` (unit-tested 4900→`"49.00"`, 5→`"0.05"`), items + `item_total` breakdown equal total. 3. Shop order created first, bound via `custom_id`/`invoice_id`, PayPal id stored UNIQUE. 4. Paid only on `COMPLETED` capture matching amount/currency/`custom_id`; `onApprove`/`CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED` never pay (tested). 5. `INSTRUMENT_DECLINED`→422 “choose another way to pay” (stays pending), `TRANSACTION_REFUSED`/other reasons returned unpaid, `PENDING`→202 awaiting webhook; mock headers never forwarded from the browser. 6. Every webhook verified before trust; non-`SUCCESS`→400, nothing changed/recorded (forged-webhook test). 7. Event ids recorded once (PK); replays→200 no-op. 8. Atomic pending→paid claim; fulfil only on 1 row changed — concurrent captures fulfil exactly once (tested). 9. No backwards moves (late APPROVED after paid is a no-op). 10. `ORDER_ALREADY_CAPTURED` and connection/timeout unknowns re-read via `getOrder` and settle from PayPal (tested both found/not-found; never marked failed). 11. `priceCart` validation: known SKUs, integer qty 1–10, rejected before any PayPal call. 12. Only the client id reaches the browser (config test asserts no secret in output or served pages).

Verification: `npm test` 22/22 pass (5 pre-existing card tests unchanged + 17 new), `node --check` clean on touched files. No live PayPal calls were made; no commit performed.

Fixed the one failed check — no commit made.

**1. Real purchase did not complete — capture `415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` (debug `ca571d11c6846`, order `FOG-1D6BB8` pending, 0 labels)**
- Root cause: `lib/paypal.js:149` called `client.orders.captureOrder({ id, payPalRequestId, prefer })` with no `body`. Per the SDK map (`node_modules/paypal/map/operations/orders.md:43`), omitting that optional body sends no body *and no `Content-Type` header at all* — the tests/fakes assumed that was fine, but the real sandbox rejects it with 415. PayPal's real answer wins over the plan's assumption.
- Fix (`lib/paypal.js`): pass `body: {}` to `captureOrder`, so the SDK sends `"{}"` with `Content-Type: application/json`. No `paymentSource` is invented — the body is otherwise empty. The settle logic (COMPLETED + amount/currency/`custom_id` match → atomic paid claim → fulfil once) is unchanged, so a captured order now fulfils; all attack paths (server-side pricing, quantity/SKU validation, forged/mismatched webhooks, `INSTRUMENT_DECLINED`/`TRANSACTION_REFUSED`, `ORDER_ALREADY_CAPTURED` re-read, concurrent-capture claims) stay as-is and are covered by existing tests.
- Test added (`test/paypal.test.js`): “capture sends empty JSON body with application/json content-type (real sandbox 415 regression)” asserts exactly one capture call with `content-type: application/json`, raw body `"{}"`, parsed body `{}`.
- Contract updated (`paypal-plan.md`): captureOrder section and the §1b.3 optional-fields table now record that `body: {}` is required (§ was: omit body key), citing the 415/debug-id evidence.

Verification: `npm test` green — 23 pass (was 22), card checkout and PayPal button flows untouched; `node --check` passes on touched files.

Per the SDK map (`node_modules/paypal/map/operations/orders.md:43`), omitting that optional body sends no body *and no `Content-Type` header at all* — the tests/fakes assumed that was fine, but the real sandbox rejects it with 415. PayPal's real answer wins over the plan's assumption.
- Fix (`lib/paypal.js`): pass `body: {}` to `captureOrder`, so the SDK sends `"{}"` with `Content-Type: application/json`. No `paymentSource` is invented — the body is otherwise empty. The settle logic (COMPLETED + amount/currency/`custom_id` match → atomic paid claim → fulfil once) is unchanged, so a captured order now fulfils; all attack paths (server-side pricing, quantity/SKU validation, forged/mismatched webhooks, `INSTRUMENT_DECLINED`/`TRANSACTION_REFUSED`, `ORDER_ALREADY_CAPTURED` re-read, concurrent-capture claims) stay as-is and are covered by existing tests.
- Test added (`test/paypal.test.js`): “capture sends empty JSON body with application/json content-type (real sandbox 415 regression)” asserts exactly one capture call with `content-type: application/json`, raw body `"{}"`, parsed body `{}`.
- Contract updated (`paypal-plan.md`): captureOrder section and the §1b.3 optional-fields table now record that `body: {}` is required (§ was: omit body key), citing the 415/debug-id evidence.

Verification: `npm test` green — 23 pass (was 22), card checkout and PayPal button flows untouched; `node --check` passes on touched files.

plans.name: Rail switch after PayPal approval
